claims.text: The starting AlCrFeNiSi powder is homogeneous and gas-atomized.
The AlCrFeNiSi powder has been sieved to a particle-size range of 10–60 μm.
The proposed intervention is to replace ambient-air debinding with oxygen-deficient debinding produced by continuous mechanical-pump evacuation.
The proposed process uses 405 nm DLP exposure at 19.57 mW/cm² for 100 s per 70 μm layer, two debinding holds, and 24 h sintering at 800–1100 °C.
Oxygen-deficient debinding retains some carbon from the acrylate resin.
Oxygen-deficient debinding causes less oxidation of the resin and AlCrFeNiSi powder than oxygen-rich debinding.
Reduced oxidation during debinding decreases rapid CO and CO2 evolution.
Reduced rapid gas evolution lowers pressure-induced surface cracking and pore formation.
Oxide layers formed on particle surfaces during oxygen-rich debinding impede interparticle diffusion.
Carbon retained after oxygen-deficient debinding facilitates earlier interparticle diffusion and bonding during sintering.
Improved interparticle diffusion and bonding permit consolidation at lower sintering temperatures.
Oxygen-deficient debinding should enable full consolidation near 1050 °C rather than 1100 °C.
At a sintering temperature approximately 50 °C lower, oxygen-deficient specimens should attain maximum compressive strength comparable to oxygen-rich specimens.
Oxygen-deficient specimens should exhibit less surface cracking than oxygen-rich specimens.
Oxygen-deficient specimens should exhibit lower porosity than oxygen-rich specimens.
Air-debound DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi requires sintering at 1100 °C to attain full densification.
Air-debound DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi reaches approximately 5.1 MPa compressive strength.
Elemental diffusion is limited below approximately 1000 °C under the stated processing conditions.
Localized softening or melting may occur near 1100 °C even after oxygen-deficient debinding.
The predicted benefits are limited to the specified DLP parameters, debinding schedule, and 24 h sintering window.
